pass_b_english: As the world unfolds in the necessary world, the wonder of Christ's name becomes apparent, and it is worth considering the theory presented in the psalm that has been placed before us.

The prophet David knew that according to the true and divine promise, Christ would be born from the fruit of his loins, and God, existing by nature, would sit among us in due time, speaking in the eighth psalm and making words to him as to a human and also to God, recognizing the one God from both.
He says, 'Lord, our Lord, how wonderful is your name in all the earth, for your magnificence has been lifted up above the heavens' (Psalm 8:1).
For where or among whom is Christ not wondered at, or how has his magnificence not been lifted up above the heavens?

If it is true that in the name of Jesus Christ every knee bends and every tongue confesses that Jesus Christ is Lord to the glory of God the Father (Philippians 2:10-11), then it is clear that Christ's name is indeed wonderful and his magnificence has been lifted up above the heavens.

When Christ raised Lazarus from the dead, all were amazed, and as he sat on a donkey, children waved palm branches and cried out 'Hosanna to the son of David, blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord' (Matthew 21:9).
The others rebuked them, but Christ said, 'Have you not read that I will perfect praise from the mouth of infants and sucklings?' (Matthew 21:16).

This event shows that even though Christ is God by nature, he humbled himself to such an extent that he allowed himself to be led by the crowd, and Paul declares that he has been stripped of the former glory, saying he has been stripped of it.
The blessed David saw the reason for this emptying and understood that it was so that Christ might rescue us from corruption and sin and the tyrannical hands of the devil.
The mystery of the economy with flesh is worthy of all wonder.
He says, 'Lord, what is man that you remember him, or the son of man that you visit him?' (Psalm 8:4).
For what is human nature in relation to God, and what is this that I say, what is human genus?
What portion is assigned to them on earth in relation to the orders of holy angels?
Even if man is nothing by nature and number, the Creator did not despise us, for he remembered us and deemed us worthy of visitation, as if we were perishing.

In the beginning, God brought us into existence, lowering us briefly below the angels, but then crowning us with honor and glory, setting us over the works of his hands, and subjecting all things under our feet.

The divine Paul skillfully sets forth the things concerning us, which have been renewed through Christ, and the scope of the whole song is in these things, appearing in the necessary world as it unfolds.
The things in Christ are a new creation, and the old things have passed away, and all things have become new.
The Holy Spirit says through one of the prophets, 'Take courage, Zion, do not let your hands weaken; the Lord your God is in you, to save you and renew you in his love' (Isaiah 41:10).
Paul declares us to be stripped of the former glory, and therefore, he says, 'Now we do not yet see all things subjected to him' (1 Corinthians 15:28).
